m:senate: The square can be seen for free at any time. Inside the cathedral entry is paid for adults: €8 from 1 September to 31 October (free under 18), with Luke Jerram's Helios exhibition on show until 1 November; the crypt is free until 31 October. Autumn hours aren't published on the page I read (in summer Monday–Thursday 9am–6pm, Friday 9am–2pm, Sunday noon–5pm): check helsingintuomiokirkko.fi. The church closes to visitors during services.
m:suomenlinna: The regular ferry runs all year from the Kauppatori (east side, in front of the Presidential Palace): it takes an AB ticket (€3.30 in the app or at the machines, €3.50 contactless) and tickets can't be bought on board. From late October there's at least one sailing an hour. The Visitor Centre is open every day 10am–4pm. Walking around the island is free; the museums (Suomenlinna Museum and Military Museum open all year, the Vesikko submarine and Ehrensvärd Museum summer only) have separate tickets, to be confirmed on suomenlinna.fi. In autumn and winter it's cold and windy and many cafés are closed: dress in layers.
m:uspenski: Closed on Mondays. Hours from a travel guide (to be confirmed on hos.fi/uspenski): Tuesday–Friday 9:30am–4pm, Saturday 9:30am–2pm, Sunday noon–3pm. Entry is free according to one guide, while another reports a €5 ticket: check the day before. No visits during religious services.
m:kauppatori: The Old Market Hall is open Monday to Saturday 8am–6pm (the guide gives Sunday 10am–5pm, to be confirmed); on Saturday 31 October it has special hours, 10am–5pm. The outdoor stalls on the square mostly operate in summer and in October many are closed or reduced. Almost all stalls take cards.
m:ateneum: Closed on Mondays. Hours: Tuesday and Friday 10am–6pm, Wednesday and Thursday 10am–8pm, Saturday and Sunday 10am–5pm (from the Finnish museums listing, museot.fi). The ticket is around €23: the listing shows «23/21/13/0 €» without saying which category applies, so check the price on ateneum.fi. Under-18s go free.
m:temppeliaukio: Open Monday–Saturday 9am–4pm, Sunday noon–5pm (museot.fi; last entry 10 minutes before closing). Ticket €8, free under 18. It's closed to visitors during weddings, baptisms, funerals and Sunday mass (10am, about an hour and a half): hours are updated weekly on temppeliaukionkirkko.fi.
m:oodi: Open Monday–Friday 8am–9pm, Saturday and Sunday 10am–8pm (oodihelsinki.fi, special hours on holidays). Entry is free; the third floor, with the café and terrace, is open to everyone.
m:kiasma: Closed on Mondays. Hours: Tuesday and Friday 10am–8pm, Wednesday and Thursday 10am–6pm, Saturday and Sunday 10am–5pm (museot.fi). The ticket is around €23: the listing shows «23/13/0 €» without specifying categories, so check the price on kiasma.fi. On Friday 6 November and Friday 4 December 2026 entry is free.
m:sibelius: The park and the monument are always accessible and free. In autumn and winter the park is dark by late afternoon. Café Regatta, a few steps away, is open all year.
m:esplanadi: The park is always open and free. Shops are usually open Monday–Friday 10am–7pm, Saturday 10am–6pm, Sunday often noon–4pm. In winter, between late November and Christmas, the Christmas lights are switched on.
vd:ekberg: Finland's oldest pâtisserie and café, open since 1861 on a tree-lined street in Punavuori: a breakfast buffet every day, cakes and fresh bread from the bakery next door, and simple Finnish dishes at lunch.
vp:ekberg: A buffet breakfast is around €15–20 and a coffee with a pastry around €8–10 (menu not seen). Summer hours (until 6 September) from ekberg.fi: in autumn they may change, to be confirmed.
vd:soppa: The soup counter in the market hall: lohikeitto, the creamy salmon soup with potatoes and chives, comes with unlimited rye bread, eaten at the little tables by the counter.
vp:soppa: A salmon soup is around €11–13 (figure from a guide, menu not seen). Hours are those of the market hall: the counter itself may close earlier, to be confirmed.
vd:regatta: A little red wooden cottage by the sea in Töölö, with an old-time country interior: freshly baked korvapuusti (cinnamon rolls), coffee and, in the yard, sausages to grill over the fire. Prices are low.
vp:regatta: A coffee with a cinnamon roll is around €7–9 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed; location approximate.
vd:aalto: The café on the first floor of the Akateeminen bookshop, in the building designed by Alvar Aalto: bright rooms with skylights, design chairs and a menu of sandwiches, soups and cakes. You can stay reading for hours with a single order.
vp:aalto: A coffee with a slice of cake is around €9–11 and a sandwich around €10–14 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide (Saturday the same as Sunday, to be confirmed).
vd:hakan: The market hall in the Kallio district, less touristy than the one at the harbour: stalls with fish, cheeses, bread and pastries, and upstairs lunch stalls with Finnish home cooking and other cuisines, at low prices.
vp:hakan: Lunch is around €10–15 (menu not seen). Open Monday to Saturday 8am–6pm; on Saturday 31 October the market hall is closed (from the market website). Individual stall hours to be confirmed.
vd:savotta: A traditional Finnish restaurant in a building overlooking Senate Square, in a wooden-cabin setting: a short menu with Nordic dishes like reindeer, lake fish and salmon soup, and local beer.
vp:savotta: A main course is around €25–35 (menu not seen: the price is an estimate). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:seahorse: A 1934 restaurant near the harbour, known to Finns for its onion steak and fish: fried Baltic herring, vorschmack and a classic Wiener schnitzel. On Wednesday to Saturday evenings the cloakroom costs €2.50 extra.
vp:seahorse: A main course is around €20–30 (menu not seen: the price is an estimate). Hours from the restaurant's website; the kitchen closes an hour and a half earlier.
vd:fazer: The historic café of the Fazer chocolate family, since 1891, a short walk from the Esplanadi: large rooms with marble tables, cakes, pastries and a rich breakfast. Fazer chocolate is sold in the shop at the entrance.
vp:fazer: A coffee with a cake is around €9–12 (menu not seen). Monday–Friday and Sunday hours from a guide; Saturday is the same as Sunday, to be confirmed.
cd:nationalmuseum: Finnish history from prehistory to today, in a neo-medieval building.
cd:amosrex: An underground museum beneath Lasipalatsi square, with domes rising out of the square.
cd:designmus: Finnish design, from Aalto to Marimekko.
cd:seurasaari: Wooden farms and churches from every region of Finland on an island.
cx:seurasaari: Open only in summer: check the calendar.
cd:loyly: A sauna with terraces on the sea, for a dip after the heat.
cd:allas: Pools and saunas on the sea, next to the market.
cd:korkeasaari: The zoo on an island, reached by ferry.
cd:canalcruise: A boat trip among the islands and fortresses off the city.
